answer: Each identity registers one reef tide-pool plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a census on a wander of the rim at nadir tide. The auditor recounts the plot against the tide table; a count over 5 percent above the filed census, a reused plot key, or one fragment counted in two plots burns the bond. The first census costs 26 credits, the kth 26+6(k-1), the 1000th 6020, so 1000 fakes pay 3,023,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-census ring fails because each plot key binds one surveyor and the nadir recount is public. An honest surveyor pays 26 once and recovers the bond after audit.
